Subject: Re: [Urgent] Production errors — initial server-side evidence

Anna / team — attaching the artifacts we pulled for the window you reported.

Summary (initial findings):
- Time window examined: 08:30–09:10 PT (05:30–06:10 UTC).
- Observed a sharp increase in queue depth on the dedicated pool's scheduler at ~08:41 PT; sustained high queue depth persisted until ~08:59 PT.
- The autoscaler attempted a scale-up, but the warmup policy (configured to prefer reserved warm nodes) delayed routing of capacity by ~90s, which increased tail latency for short-running chat requests.
- We also recorded three transient eviction events tied to host-level memory pressure; those resulted in temporary token-stream interruptions for in-flight requests.

Attachments included: scheduler_logs.zip (allocator + scheduler traces), kv_snapshot_20270523.tgz (KV cache snapshot), timeline.csv (per-second summary).

Mitigation applied today (05/23):
- Reduced warmup hold time on the affected pool to speed route-in of new capacity (temporary config change).
- Disabled a non-critical quantized variant on that pool to lower memory pressure while we investigate further.

Next steps / RCF (root cause follow-ups):
1) Deep dive on warmup policy interaction with burst routing (engineering item).
2) Memory pressure root cause (OS/kernel + model variant memory footprint).
3) Evaluate a permanent autoscaler tuning change for LEX-Prod reserved pools.

I’ve uploaded the full evidence bundle to the shared drive link (see HubSpot record). If you want the raw logs dropped in your S3, we can arrange that.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Production Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: GPU pool threshold breach — remediation timeline & credit proposal

Hi Anna — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Final summary and next steps below so procurement has what it needs to make a decision.

Short answers:
- Evictions: our evidence shows the transient evictions correlated with a larger-than-expected memory footprint on one quantized model variant (quant-8x). We temporarily disabled that variant during the mitigation window to reduce host pressure.
- Credits: Redwood distinguishes between platform defects and configuration-edge delays. Given that the warmup policy defaulted to reserved-warm behavior and that caused a measurable delay in route-in time, we accept partial responsibility. Proposed credit: 10% service credit for the affected day's usage on the dedicated pool (detailed in the attached credit_proposal.pdf). Procurement, please advise if you need a formal credit note.

Deliverables we’ve provided:
- Full evidence package: evidence_package_lexisys_20270526.zip (consolidated logs, timeline.csv, analysis.pdf) — uploaded to the drive link below.
- HubSpot incident: HS-70821 (contains timeline & artifacts).
- Action items for Redwood engineering: warmup-policy tuning for reserved pools (ETA: 3 weeks), autoscaler unit tests for warmup latency (ETA: 4 weeks), and memory profiling on quant variants (ETA: 2 weeks).

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/lexisys/evidence-20270523
HubSpot: HS-70821

If that credit estimate looks reasonable, Ben (cc) will run the paperwork and we can schedule a short sync for any follow-up. Apologies again for the impact — we’re prioritizing a permanent fix.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
